findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a concrete pass criterion for the undimensioned-vs-per-ModelId re-verification (e.g. exact equality over a fresh N-day window) and a fallback if it fails (block the story / fall back to per-ModelId sum).
evidence: 'Over 2026-09-14 to 09-24 it equalled the per-ModelId sum exactly, 930,831,660 tokens both ways; re-verify before relying on it.'
No AC covers the re-verification; 're-verify before relying on it' defers the pass/fail decision and any remediation to the executor with no stated threshold or fallback path.
findings.finding: The trip-side estimate depends entirely on the AWS/Bedrock zero-dimension token series equalling the per-ModelId sum, an unverified external-system assumption. The plan says 're-verify before relying on it' but states no success criterion for that re-verification and no fallback if the equivalence no longer holds (e.g. a new service publishing only per-ModelId series would make the undimensioned read under-count, weakening the cap).
findings.location: Approach — 'AWS/Bedrock publishes a zero-dimension series per token metric... re-verify before relying on it.'
scenarios: Re-verification at implement time shows the undimensioned series now diverges from the per-ModelId sum because a newly live service publishes only per-ModelId metrics
Executor cannot decide whether a small divergence is acceptable
findings.suggested_fix: Add an acceptance criterion: 're-run the undimensioned-vs-per-ModelId comparison over a fresh 10-day window; require exact equality; if it diverges, halt and escalate rather than shipping the undimensioned read.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Route the zero-dimension AWS/Bedrock aggregate-series assumption through an explicit verification/SPIKE gate before the estimate depends on it (e.g. an AC that a Dimensions:[] GetMetricData read returns non-empty datapoints equal to the per-ModelId Sum on this account), and specify the handler behaviour if the aggregate series is found absent so an empty read cannot silently disable the fast signal.
evidence: Plan: 'AWS/Bedrock publishes a zero-dimension series per token metric, requested by sending Dimensions: [] (omitting the key is not equivalent).'
Plan: 'Over 2026-09-14 to 09-24 it equalled the per-ModelId sum exactly, 930,831,660 tokens both ways; re-verify before relying on it.' — Partially-verified, not Verified.

handler.py:418 today filters to per-ModelId series (`len(dims) != 1 or dims[0]['Name'] != 'ModelId'`) and comments the undimensioned aggregate 'would double-count' — the aggregate has never been read, so this is a new surface.

CloudWatch GetMetricData does not synthesize an across-dimension aggregate; the zero-dimension series must be published by the vendor. The claim it exists and equals the ModelId sum is the load-bearing assumption.

Neither this story nor the dependent be3d-712b-c1ac-442b records a fixture proving the undimensioned aggregate exists or equals the sum; be3d's recorded fixture is a list_metrics ModelId corpus, which this story stops using.
findings.finding: The ceiling-estimate arm depends on an unverified new CloudWatch surface — a zero-dimension AWS/Bedrock aggregate series queried with Dimensions: [] — that the handler has never used (today it reads only per-ModelId series and treats the aggregate as double-counting). The plan cites an 11-day empirical equality but marks it 're-verify before relying on it' and does not gate the change behind that verification; if the aggregate series does not exist as published, an empty read yields a zero estimate that silently disables the fast signal, which is the 'cap fires late' failure this story exists to prevent.
findings.location: Approach — 'AWS/Bedrock publishes a zero-dimension series per token metric, requested by sending Dimensions: [] ... re-verify before relying on it.'; AC 'issues exactly four undimensioned GetMetricData queries per region, each sending Dimensions: []'
scenarios: The account's AWS/Bedrock metrics publish only per-ModelId (and other dimensioned) series, so a Dimensions:[] query returns no datapoints; the ceiling estimate is silently zero and enforcement relies on CE alone, which lags 8-24h — the exact late-fire failure being removed.
The zero-dimension series exists but does not equal the per-ModelId sum (e.g. excludes a provider or region), so the ceiling under-counts.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the same-tick ordering for the fresh-UTC-day release: specify whether the release decision uses the mark value after this tick writes today's zero mark (immediate release) or before (one-tick hold), so a new day with a stale deny and no traffic releases as intended.
evidence: Plan: 'keyed by UTC date so a new day starts absent'
Plan: 'An empty read may release only when today's key is present and zero-valued; an absent key with a deny attached holds the deny'
Current handler releases the same tick: `if any_attached and spend < THRESHOLD_USD and not signal_unavailable: _apply(attach=False)` with no mark gate (handler.py:718)
bedrock_spend_cap.tf:462 — the tick rule 'also performs the 00:00 UTC release'
findings.finding: The release discriminator does not specify whether, on the first tick of a new UTC day with a deny still attached and an empty CloudWatch read, the deny releases in the same tick that writes today's zero mark or only on the following tick. Because 'a new day starts absent' and 'an absent key with a deny attached holds the deny', a literal read of the rules holds yesterday's deny for one 5-minute tick into the new day, changing the current instant-at-00:00-UTC automatic release.
findings.location: Approach -> Release discriminator; ACs 'The day's high-water token total is persisted keyed by UTC date' and 'An empty read with today's key present and zero-valued may release'
scenarios: 00:00 UTC rolls over while yesterday's deny is still attached and there is no traffic yet: first tick sees an absent key + empty read
A mid-day deploy over old state where the deny should be held vs. a genuine new-day release — the two must be distinguished by the same mark logic
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that on an empty read the handler writes today's zero-valued key first, then evaluates release against the just-written key, so a fresh day with a stale attached deny releases on the first tick — while a nonzero mark or a surviving-region floor still holds it.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the RETIRE path for the high-water mark: state how stale UTC-date keys are pruned (e.g. keep only today's key on write, or TTL) so the store does not accumulate a key per day forever.
evidence: 'the handler persists the day's highest observed token total, keyed by UTC date so a new day starts absent'
ABSENCE: no acceptance criterion or approach sentence describes deleting/expiring yesterday's key
findings.finding: The day's high-water token total is persisted keyed by UTC date, but the plan specifies no RETIRE/cleanup path for stale date keys — each UTC day adds a new key and old keys are never pruned, so the state store accumulates unboundedly.
findings.location: Approach — 'Release discriminator' paragraph; AC 'The day's high-water token total is persisted keyed by UTC date.'
findings.suggested_fix: On each write, replace the whole mark with a single {utc_date: high_water} entry (or delete keys older than today), and add an AC asserting only the current day's key survives.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the concurrency model for the high-water mark update (single-flight invocation, or an atomic max/conditional write) so a concurrent invocation cannot regress the recorded floor.
evidence: 'persists the day's highest observed token total, keyed by UTC date'
ABSENCE: no mention of atomic update, conditional write, lock/CAS, or single-invocation guarantee for the mark
findings.finding: The high-water mark is a read-modify-write on shared persisted state, but the plan does not state how concurrent Lambda invocations updating it are serialized. If two invocations both read a lower value and one writes a higher then the other overwrites with the lower, the floor guarantee the release logic depends on can be violated.
findings.location: Approach — 'Release discriminator': 'the handler persists the day's highest observed token total'
findings.suggested_fix: Use a conditional/atomic max update (write only if new total exceeds stored) or confirm the Lambda's reserved concurrency is 1, and add an AC covering the concurrent-update case.

findings.checklist_item: State what the reverted handler does when it first reads state written by the new code (missing rates/rates_day, extra high-water key) — confirm old code self-heals (re-derives rates, ignores unknown keys) so rollback leaves enforcement correct, not merely 'code restored'.
evidence: Rollback: 'the revert restores prior code, env and IAM exactly' — asserts code/env/IAM restoration, not post-rollback state interpretation.

The plan removes read paths for state["rates"]/state["rates_day"] and adds a new persisted key, matching the POST-ROLLBACK STATE trigger 'removes or narrows a read path' and 'changes how existing persisted records are interpreted'.
The state is a single tolerant JSON blob (_load_state returns {} on corrupt/missing and reads keys via .get), so residual/missing keys are likely benign — but the plan does not say so.
findings.finding: The Rollback section asserts the revert 'restores prior code, env and IAM exactly' but does not assert on the persisted SSM state AFTER rollback. The change narrows read paths (removes state["rates"]/state["rates_day"]/metered_estimated) and changes release interpretation via a new UTC-date-keyed high-water key, so after a revert the reverted handler reads state the new code wrote (lacking the rates keys, carrying an unknown high-water key). The plan does not state that the reverted handler tolerates/self-heals this (e.g. re-derives rates and ignores unknown keys).
findings.location: Rollback section; ACs 'The day's high-water token total is persisted keyed by UTC date' and 'state["rates"], state["rates_day"], metered_estimated ... are removed'
scenarios: Operator reverts the Gerrit change mid-day; the reverted (old) handler's first read encounters state written by the new code with no 'rates'/'rates_day' and an extra high-water key.
A revert immediately after a new-code trip, where release/enforcement must resume correctly from the mutated state.
